question: Should this defense-in-depth guard be accepted without a production-client baseline that reproduces overlap past the existing REST timeout?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically reasonable, but the current evidence does not establish that the claimed production overlap can occur through the real client contract, so accepting the additional guard requires maintainer judgment about proof and scope.

options.title: Require like-for-like baseline
options.body: Ask for a controlled current-main run through the production REST client that crosses the 120-second interval and then shows the exact-head guard preventing overlap.

options.title: Accept defense in depth
options.body: Accept the guard and explicit timeout as low-risk hardening despite the missing production-contract baseline.

options.title: Narrow to timeout only
options.body: Remove the single-flight helper if the real client timeout already makes cross-tick REST overlap unreachable and retain only the demonstrated timeout repair.

recommendation.title: Require like-for-like baseline
recommendation.body: Ask for a controlled current-main run through the production REST client that crosses the 120-second interval and then shows the exact-head guard preventing overlap.
